stem: How many profiles can a user have?

options.text: Exactly one
Up to three
As many as needed
None if they have a permission set

explanation: Every user must have exactly one profile. Extra access is added with permission sets.

stem: How many permission sets can be assigned to one user?

options.text: Many
Only one
None
Exactly two

explanation: A user can be assigned many permission sets, which only add access.

stem: Which setting exists only on profiles and not on permission sets?

options.text: Login hours
Object Read permission
Field-level security
System permissions

explanation: Login hours and login IP ranges are profile-only settings.

stem: What is the recommended approach to granting access under least privilege?

options.text: A minimal base profile plus permission sets for needed access
Give everyone the System Administrator profile
Clone a profile for every individual
Give View All Data to team leads

explanation: Least privilege means a minimal base access and then adding only what each role needs, usually through permission sets.

stem: What is a permission set group used for?

options.text: Bundling permission sets for a job role so one assignment grants them all
Replacing the role hierarchy for the whole org
Setting the organization-wide defaults for each object
Limiting login hours for a group of users

explanation: A permission set group packages related permission sets so you assign them together.

stem: What does muting a permission inside a permission set group do?

options.text: Removes it only within that group
Removes it from the underlying permission set for everyone
Deletes the permission set
Locks the user's account

explanation: Muting applies only inside the group and leaves the source permission set unchanged elsewhere.

stem: Where is a user's default record type set?

options.text: On the profile
On the permission set
On the role
On the sharing rule

explanation: The default record type is a profile setting. Permission sets can add record types but not set the default.

stem: In Setup you tick Delete on an object inside a permission set. What does Salesforce enable automatically?

options.text: Read and Edit, because Delete depends on both
Create only
View All
Nothing, the admin must tick the other permissions by hand

explanation: Delete depends on Read and Edit, so Salesforce turns those on for you. View All and Create are not required for Delete.

stem: Which TWO object permissions must a user also have in order to Delete records? (Choose 2)

options.text: Read
Edit
Create
View All

explanation: Delete depends on Read and Edit. Create and View All are not required for Delete.

stem: A user needs to see every Installation record regardless of sharing. What should they be granted?

options.text: View All on the Installation object
Read on the Installation object only
A manual share on each record
A new role

explanation: View All on an object lets the user see all its records and bypasses sharing for that object.

stem: What does the Modify All Data system permission do?

options.text: Gives full access to all records in all objects and bypasses sharing
Allows users to log in at any hour of the day
Allows only data exports, with no changes to records
Lets the user change the name of the org in Setup

explanation: Modify All Data is extremely powerful: it lets a user view, edit and delete all data in the org regardless of sharing.

stem: Which control hides a field from a user in reports and the API as well as on record pages?

options.text: Field-level security
Removing it from the page layout
Removing it from the compact layout
Renaming the field

explanation: Only field-level security truly hides the field everywhere. Layout changes affect only that screen.

stem: What is the difference between freezing and deactivating a user?

options.text: Freezing blocks login but keeps the licence in use; deactivating frees the licence
Freezing deletes the user while deactivating only hides them
Freezing frees the licence while deactivating keeps it in use
There is no difference, because both stop the user logging in

explanation: Freeze is a quick stop on login without freeing the licence. Deactivation removes the user's ability to log in and frees the licence.

stem: A person has left Khanyisa Solar. What should the admin do with their user record?

options.text: Deactivate it
Delete it
Rename it
Change their profile to Standard User

explanation: Users cannot be deleted. Deactivating blocks access and frees the licence while preserving history.

stem: Which of these can a queue own?

options.text: Leads and Cases
Accounts
Opportunities
Dashboards

explanation: Queues can own records such as Leads, Cases and custom objects. They cannot own Accounts or Opportunities.

stem: A user can open an Installation record but cannot see the Discount field. What should you check first?

options.text: Field-level security on their profile and permission sets
The org's login hours for the user's profile
The organization-wide default of the Installation object
The role hierarchy position of the user's manager

explanation: If the record is visible but one field is not, the issue is field access, so check FLS across the profile and all permission sets.

stem: What is the most reliable way to see exactly what a user sees without knowing their password?

options.text: Log in as that user
Ask for a screenshot
Compare their profile to yours
Clone their user record

explanation: Logging in as the user shows their real experience. This requires the org's login-as setting or user-granted access.

stem: Most standard profiles can only be changed in a few settings. What is the right way to customise one?

options.text: Clone it into a custom profile
Edit it directly
Delete it and recreate it
Use the role hierarchy

explanation: Standard profiles are largely locked, so clone one into a custom profile to customise it.

stem: Which statement about permission sets is true (outside of muting in a group)?

options.text: They only add access and never take access away
They can remove access given by the profile
They replace the profile
They apply only to Administrators

explanation: Permission sets are additive. To remove access you change the profile or the permission set, or mute inside a group.

stem: Two users have the same profile but only one can open a particular Installation. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: Record access differs, such as ownership, role or sharing
Their page layout differs
Their browsers differ
The Installation object permission differs because the profiles are the same

explanation: If a peer with the same profile and the same permission sets can open the record, object permissions are the same, so the difference is at the record level: ownership, role hierarchy or sharing. (Permission sets can also differ between users, so confirm they match first.)

stem: An admin wants the same access for all new Sales Reps and a clear audit trail of why they have it. What is the best design?

options.text: A permission set group for the Sales Rep job role
A new custom profile cloned for each person
Giving everyone the System Administrator profile temporarily
Individual manual shares

explanation: A permission set group gives a single, auditable assignment per role and keeps access aligned with least privilege.

stem: A user cannot see any Installation records but peers in the same role can. Everyone has the same OWD. What is the best next check?

options.text: The user's object Read permission on Installation via profile and permission sets
The org's currency settings, which hide records in other currencies
The email address on the user, which is matched to the owner
The Chatter settings that decide which feeds the user can see

explanation: If a peer can see records, record access is probably fine, so check whether the user has Read on the object through their profile or permission sets.

stem: A sales rep can open Installation records but the Discount field does not appear on the page or in reports. The page layout includes the field. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: Field-level security hides the field from the rep
The record type is wrong for that rep's profile
The OWD is Private, so the field is hidden
The rep's role is too low in the hierarchy

explanation: If a field is on the layout but still hidden, check field-level security on the profile and permission sets.

stem: Finance needs to read every Installation record but must not edit anything, and no new role can be created. Which is the best option?

options.text: A permission set with View All on Installation
A sharing rule to the Finance profile
Modify All Data on the profile
A new page layout

explanation: View All on the object lets users read all records without a role change. Profiles are not sharing targets, and Modify All Data is far too wide.
